research_question: What additional architecture is actually required to capture explicit author choices safely, accessibly and without transferring authority to AI/providers or duplicating the existing Book lifecycle, integration and versioning engines?

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.finding: Human-AI configurations vary; systems may defer decisions to humans, and human-AI interaction can amplify human biases. Human oversight must be designed for context rather than assumed to be automatically effective.

sources.title: AI RMF Playbook / AIRC Core
sources.finding: Roles and responsibilities for human-AI oversight should be explicitly differentiated and oversight processes defined, assessed and documented.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
sources.finding: Generative AI may require additional human review, tracking, documentation and management oversight; accessibility and change-management controls are relevant governance tools.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2
sources.finding: Consequential submissions that modify stored user data should provide reversibility, error checking, or a review/confirmation/correction opportunity; redundant entry should be avoided where possible.

sources.title: Technique G168: Requesting confirmation to continue with selected action
sources.finding: For irreversible actions, confirmation should identify the selected action and consequences so the user can stop an unintended submission.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines — Action sheets
sources.finding: Use action sheets for choices related to an intentional action; provide Cancel where needed; make destructive choices clear; avoid scrolling; on Apple Watch keep choices especially small, and on iOS use compact choice surfaces rather than overloaded menus.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines — Alerts
sources.finding: Use alerts sparingly for essential actionable information; uncommon irreversible destructive actions merit confirmation; avoid making destructive actions the default.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines — Accessibility / Buttons
sources.finding: iOS/iPadOS controls should generally provide a 44x44 pt default target, with sufficient spacing to reduce accidental activation.

sources.title: Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) Version 2.0 — User Task
sources.finding: A User Task has an explicit actual human owner/performer and leaves rendering technology open; useful as a conceptual role-separation reference, not a reason to add a BPMN engine.

classifications.reason: It already represents the durable author-authority evidence consumed by Lifecycle and other parent gates.

classifications.item: Runtime V2 author_handoff as a request source
classifications.reason: It already queues author requirements while explicitly lacking resolution authority.
It is already qualified and correctly fail-closed.
It preserves author-decision successors without transferring author authority into versioning.
Pending requests, presentation, staleness, dedup, resolution concurrency and receipts are not represented by the current canonical AUTHOR_DECISION object.
Every pending item must bind exact object/version/digest and parent-state version/digest so a choice cannot silently apply to changed prose, canon, proposal, artifact or publication candidate.

NIST notes human-AI interaction can amplify bias. AI/provider-preferred options therefore cannot silently become defaults. Each option requires stable option_id, plain-language effect/consequence, evidence refs where relevant, and explicit custom-author-option support when the decision contract allows it.

WCAG error-prevention guidance supports review/confirmation/correction before final submission where the action changes stored data or has serious consequences. High-impact author decisions should present the exact selected option and consequence before the immutable decision commit.

The queue data layer should expose concise title, decision question, options, consequences, evidence summary, safe cancel/defer and confirmation requirements so the System Master iPhone UI can render accessible controls. Target UI should use at least 44x44 pt hit regions, visible focus/accessibility labels, and avoid overloaded scrolling action sheets.

If subject identity or material options change, the old request remains historical but cannot be resolved for the changed subject. Corrections after an immutable author decision create a new/superseding decision, never edit the old choice.
NIST and BPMN both support clear human-role ownership. AUTHOR_ONLY must be distinct from external/legal and parent-operational authorities.
User-task role concepts are useful but Book already has lifecycle/integration/versioning machinery; a generic workflow engine would duplicate authority and scope.

classifications.item: Auto-approval, timeout-approval, majority vote or AI-preferred default
classifications.reason: These would manufacture or steer author authority rather than capture it. Timeout may create reminder/escalation/defer state only, never approval.
Resolution may append one AUTHOR_DECISION only. Existing qualified authorities independently consume it afterward.

classifications.item: Hard-code Apple UI components into Book runtime
classifications.reason: Book owns decision semantics/projection; System Master Core/app layer owns actual iPhone presentation.

bound_implementation_decisions.timeout_rule: No automatic resolution. Time may drive reminder/escalation metadata only.
bound_implementation_decisions.staleness_rule: Any material bound subject/version/digest, option set, authority requirement, rights/privacy or governing-constraint change prevents resolution until a new/current queue snapshot is explicitly produced.
bound_implementation_decisions.resolution_commit_scope: Append exactly one immutable canonical AUTHOR_DECISION plus queue/receipt state. Do not advance lifecycle, promote manuscript, admit proposal, freeze export or publish in the same authority operation.
bound_implementation_decisions.post_resolution_rule: Consumers independently validate the exact AUTHOR_DECISION against current state; Version/Rollback records the already-committed author-decision successor using exact authority receipt identity.
bound_implementation_decisions.custom_option_rule: Custom author input is permitted only when the decision type allows OPEN_OR_CUSTOM choice; it is preserved verbatim or through an explicitly defined normalized representation and cannot be silently mapped to a model-preferred predefined option.
bound_implementation_decisions.confirmation_rule: Consequential irreversible or publication-affecting choices require an explicit review/confirm step that states selected choice and material consequence before commit.
bound_implementation_decisions.ui_projection_rule: Data contract must support a compact iPhone decision card with selectable answer controls plus custom option where allowed, evidence/details disclosure, defer/cancel and consequence confirmation; actual UI remains outside Book runtime.

qualification_effect: NONE. Research closure only; no queue runtime, human choice, canonical state change or publication authority is created.
